newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Adelaide to raise A$40 mln in note issue.
newsitem.headline: Adelaide to raise A$40 mln in note issue.

text.p: Adelaide Bank Ltd said on Friday it would issue 400,000 capital notes at A$100 each to raise A$40 million.
The issue of the notes, which mature on July 15, 2009 and offer a 8.4 percent annual interest rate, would open on May 8 and remain open until May 23 unlesssclosed earlier by the bank.
The minimum issue of the notes is 500, allowing entry for investors with A$5,000, Adelaide Bank said.
"It is an issue which should appeal to small investors, retirees and mums and dads," Adelaide Bank Managing Director Barry Fitzpatrick said in a statement.
The notes, which are being underwritten by Adelaide-based broker Day Cutten Ltd, have an 8.4 percent interest rate for the first seven years.
After that, the rate will be calculated at the 90 day bank bill rate plus 1.25 percent, determined at the start of each quarter.
The notes will be listed on the stock exchange and will be classified as Tier Two capital under Reserve Bank of Australia capital adequacy guidelines.
Adelaide Bank's shares were down two cents at A$4.27 at 2.15 p.m. (0415 GMT).
